title: Japan 40-Year JGB auction (¥300bn reopening) — the next read on super-long demand after 09-15
source: EST: mof.go.jp English September 2026 auction calendar (policy/jgbs/auction/calendar/2609e.htm), fetched direct 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 25,423 bytes), whose table row reads 'Sep. 29, 2026 | 40-year'. The issue number and offering amount are blank on the calendar because MOF's own note on that page states 'Each issue amount will be announced about one week prior to each auction date' — so the ~09-22 announcement is the confirming primary, not this page. The ¥300bn anticipated size and the reopening read come from a second MOF primary, the Auction Results for JGBs workbook (english/policy/jgbs/auction/past_auction_results/Auction_Results_for_JGBs.xls, downloaded 2026-09-08): the 40-year runs bi-monthly, issue 19 (3.8% coupon, maturity 2066-03-20) was first sold 2026-05-27 at ¥300bn and reopened 2026-07-22 at ¥300bn, making 09-29 the second reopening of issue 19 at the same size. Filed `estimate` on two counts: the size is anticipated rather than announced, and market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a non-US sovereign debt office. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: Discovered during the jgb-20y-auction-2026-09-15 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-08) on MOF's own September calendar. It earns a slot on exactly one term: it is the venue where this calendar's super-long-JGB-demand question gets its NEXT observation after 09-15, and the 40-year is the tenor where MOF's issuance cuts are deepest — ¥500bn (2025-05-28) to ¥400bn (from 2025-07-23) to ¥300bn (from 2026-05-27), a 40% reduction in twelve months, against the 20-year's ¥1,000bn to ¥800bn to ¥700bn (30%). Cover ratios across that cut: 2.21 (2025-05) · 2.13 · 2.60 · 2.59 · 2.76 · 2.54 · 2.70 · 2.82 (2026-07-22) — rising as size fell, which is the supply-managed reading the 09-15 ledger tests. It also sits in the corridor of tracked month-end prints (consumer-confidence-2026-09-29, fhfa-hpi-2026-09-29, chicago-pmi-2026-09-30, adp-employment-2026-09-30) and eleven days after boj-decision-2026-09-18, so it is the first super-long auction to price a post-decision policy rate. NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED and impact is `low` for the same reasons as the 09-15 entry: no tracked symbol carries yen-rates exposure and the measured JGB-to-US-long-end spillover is a null (n=44, t=+0.80). Estimate widens caution only.
